source.filename: A Novel Model for Layer Jamming-based Continuum Robots.pdf

constitutive_assumptions: Mass change of air inside the airtight membrane during vacuum pressure variation is negligible, keeping the gravitational parameter constant (Assumption 1a).
The structural elastic coefficient is positive and constant during pressure variation (Assumption 1b).
Robot energy dissipation arises exclusively from the lumped friction torque, with the damping matrix set to zero (Assumption 2).
Negative pressure along the layer is uniformly distributed and linearly proportional to the lumped normal force (Assumption 3).
All functions and mappings are assumed to be C2-continuous.
Internal friction parameters satisfy the passivity inequality constraint sigma2 > sigma1 * (muS - muC) / muC, ensuring positive semi-definiteness of the friction damping matrix.
control_variables: Number of jamming sheath layers (5 layers in stiffness testing)
Bending angle prior to actuation release in shape-locking tests (60 degrees)
Repetition count under identical testing conditions (3 trials)
dependent_variables: Positional displacement / shape retention error after actuator release
Stability and convergence of the equilibria manifold

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Layer jamming utilizes overlapping thin plastic or paper sheets enclosed in an airtight membrane where vacuum pressure modulates interlayer friction to produce variable stiffness.

The dynamical behavior of a layer jamming-based, tendon-driven continuum robot can be formulated in port-Hamiltonian form by coupling an energy-based rigid link mechanical model with the LuGre friction model.
The equilibria manifold corresponding to shape locking under constant negative pressure without external actuation is locally asymptotically stable via LaSalle's invariance principle.
The linearized open-loop stiffness matrix at the equilibrium is analytically expressed as a constant structural matrix plus a term directly proportional to the vacuum pressure.
Transverse stiffness measured at the end-effector exhibits a linear correlation with negative pressure, yielding KT = 0.0046*uP + 0.3068 with a determination coefficient of R^2_s = 0.8083.
Shape locking preserves a 60-degree bending configuration upon tendon release, with higher negative pressure reducing steady-state position displacement from 9.2 mm at 30 kPa to 3.8 mm at 80 kPa.

experimental_setup: OctRobot-I continuum robotic platform configured with motor-driven tendon actuation.
Airtight membrane containing a jamming sheath composed of 5 overlapping layers installed over the robot spine.
Transverse stiffness testing apparatus at the end-effector around the open-loop equilibrium under varying negative pressure from 0 to 80 kPa, repeated three times.

Four-phase shape-locking sequence: Phase 1 (initial unactuated state), Phase 2 (tendon driven to 60-degree bending), Phase 3 (vacuum applied at 30 kPa or 80 kPa while holding motor drive), and Phase 4 (vacuum retained while releasing tendon force to zero).
Visual tracking and photographic overlay to measure positional shifts between Phase 3 and Phase 4.
future_work: Synthesizing model-based feedback controllers based on the proposed control-oriented port-Hamiltonian framework.
Revisiting and refining Assumption 3 concerning the relationship between negative pressure and lumped normal force to improve stiffness prediction accuracy.
independent_variables: Negative vacuum pressure uP (tested across 0 to 80 kPa; specifically compared at 30 kPa and 80 kPa)
External perturbation / displacement around the equilibrium configuration
limitations_inferred: The experimental validation was conducted solely on planar 2D bending up to 60 degrees, leaving 3D spatial bending, torsion, and multi-segment interaction unverified.
Dynamic tracking, cyclic loading, and hysteresis effects during repeated jamming-unjamming transitions were not evaluated.
Assumptions of constant elasticity and negligible membrane mass omit potential non-linear elastomer stretching or material wear under prolonged vacuum cycling.
limitations_stated_by_authors: The overall stiffness matrix K cannot be directly measured experimentally; only transverse stiffness KT at the end-effector could be detected.
The assumed direct proportionality between vacuum pressure and lumped normal force (Assumption 3) requires revision to improve model fitting precision.
The proposed model is oriented toward control design, but closed-loop feedback controller synthesis was not implemented in this study.
main_results: Formulated the first control-oriented port-Hamiltonian dynamical model for layer jamming-based continuum robots combining rigid-link dynamics and the LuGre friction model.
Mathematically proved that shape locking corresponds to a locally asymptotically stable equilibria manifold under constant vacuum pressure.
Analytically established that robot open-loop stiffness scales linearly with applied vacuum pressure: K = alpha1*1_nxn + [alpha2 + sigma0*uP]*In.
Empirically demonstrated a linear relationship between end-effector transverse stiffness and negative pressure (R^2_s = 0.8083, KT = 0.0046*uP + 0.3068 N/mm).
Empirically confirmed that higher vacuum pressure significantly suppresses relaxation displacement during shape locking (3.8 mm at 80 kPa compared to 9.2 mm at 30 kPa).
modeling_methods: Energy-based Hamiltonian mechanics with rigid link approximation
LuGre dynamic friction model with virtual bristle deflection
LaSalle's invariance principle for local asymptotic stability analysis
Euler-Lagrange reformulation and Jacobian linearization for open-loop stiffness derivation
performance_metrics: Coefficient of determination (R^2_s) for stiffness linearity with pressure
Positional deviation / displacement during shape locking (in mm)
possible_gap_implications: Providing a control-oriented port-Hamiltonian model enables model-based feedback control synthesis for layer-jamming continuum robots, but controller performance will depend on addressing non-linearities in normal force distribution and multi-axis deformations.
paper.research_objective: To develop a control-oriented dynamical model for layer jamming-based, tendon-driven continuum robots integrating energy-based modeling with the LuGre friction model, and to theoretically analyze and experimentally validate shape locking and adjustable stiffness.
paper.research_problem: Lack of a control-oriented dynamical model capable of approximating and predicting the dynamical behaviors (specifically shape locking and adjustable stiffness) of layer jamming-based continuum robots with variable stiffness.
paper.title: A Novel Model for Layer Jamming-based Continuum Robots
